correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the equality-partition bijection: each set partition of [n] into k blocks is labelled by (m)_k injective block assignments. A first repeat at t<=n chooses one of t-1 existing blocks; deleting that repeated index bijects to a partition of [n-1] with its first t-1 elements in distinct blocks. The terminal no-repeat case contributes only H(n+1,n)=1. The restricted count S_r(N,k) has a weighted lattice-path realization from (r,r) to (N,k), using stay transitions of weight j and increase transitions of weight 1. The Lindström–Gessel–Viennot tail-swapping involution cancels intersecting families, and inverted source/sink assignments cannot be nonintersecting: at later source time the earlier path is no higher and at the terminal time must overtake the inverted sink, forcing a shared vertex. All minors are sums of nonnegative weights. Positive row scalings and a last row supported solely in the final column preserve minors by positive Laplace expansion. Column normalization gives conditional likelihood-ratio ordering and inverse-CDF monotone coupling. Independent exhaustive set-partition enumeration and exact determinants checked ALL 1,267 square minors for n<=6; that is corroboration of the all-n planar-network proof, not its substitute.

value.rationale: The joint birthday-collision versus final richness question is a natural stochastic-dependence problem. Identifying the complete all-order totally nonnegative kernel yields likelihood-ratio ordering, stronger than just a correlation sign or mean monotonicity, for every n and uniform alphabet size. Although planar path determinant theory is standard, its exact application to this varying-initial-distinguished-label restricted-Stirling array and probabilistic interpretation is a substantive reusable structural fact.

final_claim: For n>=2, m>=n uniform iid samples, K distinct sampled symbols and first repeat time T (n+1 if none), the normalized joint count H_n(t,k)=m^n P(T=t,K=k)/(m)_k is independent of m, equals (t-1) S_{t-1}(n-1,k) for 2<=t<=n with a final unit row at (n+1,n), and every increasing square minor of H_n is nonnegative. The conditional first-repeat distributions increase with K in likelihood-ratio order.
limitations: Assumes exactly uniform iid sampling with m>=n; probability normalizations (m)_k are valid for 1<=k<=n.
